$comment: Guard-pair RESIDUE. The pairs themselves are DERIVED: .hooks/lib/guarded-data-scan.mjs parses every suite in the repo (acorn for JS, Python's own `ast` for pytest) and reports which files each one reads — by import, by resolved path, by `git ls-files`/`readdirSync` enumeration, and by `REPO_ROOT / "…"`. .hooks/run-guard-pairs.mjs runs that scan on every commit and executes the suites covering the staged files. This file holds only the two things a scan cannot decide, and test/guard-pairs.test.mjs checks both against it so an entry cannot outlive its reason. These are GUARDS, not an SSOT: a pair says "run this check when that file changes", and naming it otherwise would launder the very smell a drift guard should expose. `pairs` is for files the scan genuinely cannot chain to a test — a generator's input data, which reaches a suite only through the generated module. Adding an entry the scan already covers is an error, not a belt-and-braces: a hand-written second copy is exactly what went stale before. `tooSlowForCommit` is a cost decision, not a coverage one: the named suite still guards its sources in CI, it just does not run in the hook. The threshold is ~15s for a single suite, which is where the already-tolerated scripts/version-bump.test.mjs (12.7s) sits; measured worst-case commit today is ~29s, for an edit to src/view-map.mjs. A guard test is either a `node --test` file (*.test.mjs) or a pytest module (test_*.py); the runner dispatches on the extension, so data whose only contract test is Python is covered too.

tooSlowForCommit.plugin/test/plugin-bundle.test.mjs: 35.6s: stages the whole plugin and provisions a Python venv
tooSlowForCommit.test/hook-latency.test.mjs: measures wall-clock budgets, which the hook's own parallel batch of ~1800 tests on a shared machine makes it fail
